what: Roivant Sciences develops medicines by creating separate subsidiary companies, each focused on one drug, and then selling or partnering them. Its lead compound brepocitinib is under regulatory review for a rare muscle and skin disease.
customers: None at scale yet: its future customers would be health systems and specialists treating autoimmune disease.
money: it has essentially no product revenue
moat: A model of in-licensing promising compounds large companies have shelved and developing them quickly in small, focused subsidiaries, with a record of selling them profitably.
risks: It has no significant product revenue and loses money
Its value depends on a small number of clinical and regulatory outcomes
Revenue fell as collaboration payments ended
Developing and launching a medicine on its own is expensive and unproven for it
opportunities: Cash of about $4.2 billion against almost no debt funds it for years
Analysts see about 30% upside from current levels
A sale of a subsidiary to a large pharmaceutical company has produced large gains before
watch: The regulatory decision on brepocitinib and the cash runway.
